title: The $3,000 Credit Card Trap Hidden in Plain Sight

beats.say: A $3,000 balance can easily outlast your car, your job, and your phone.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a rusted compact car parked on wet asphalt under flickering blue hour streetlights.

beats.say: If you carry $3,000 at 24% APR, making minimum payments feels like making real progress.
beats.visual: High angle silhouette of a person standing at a cold fluorescent illuminated ATM in an empty city underpass.

beats.say: So why does your balance barely shrink after paying month after month for a full year?
beats.visual: Extreme close up on dark gloved hands sliding a blank metal card across a counter in dim sodium light.

beats.say: Most people assume paying the required statement minimum steadily wipes out what they originally borrowed.
beats.visual: Fog cutting across a dark city skyline with massive steel bridge cables stretching into the haze.

beats.say: But the actual math proves otherwise.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a lone pedestrian walking along a massive concrete rain-slick boulevard at night.

beats.say: That minimum payment is calculated as just 1% of your principal plus the monthly interest.
beats.visual: Single practical desk lamp illuminating a quiet room with heavy rain streaming down a dark windowpane.

beats.say: At 24% APR, paying only that minimum keeps you trapped for 183 long months.
beats.visual: Wet asphalt reflects yellow street lights while dark office towers loom in cold morning fog.

beats.say: That's over 15 years of endless payments for a simple $3,000 balance.
beats.visual: High angle view of an empty subway platform under pale fluorescent lights at midnight.

beats.say: Along the way, you'll hand over $4,887 in interest alone on that original debt.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a figure looking out over an expanse of shipping containers at a dark misty port.

beats.say: But if you pay $300 a month instead, that exact same balance vanishes in just 12 months.
beats.visual: Cold sodium light casting long shadows across an empty wet industrial parking lot.

beats.say: You pay just $381 in total interest, saving $4,506 in wasted finance charges.
beats.visual: Ridge line silhouette against a deep twilight sky with distant city lights glowing below.

beats.say: Raising your monthly payment breaks the trap before a balance outlasts your car, job, or phone.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of wet pavement reflecting red tail lights on an empty late night highway.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Tiny human figure walking towards a vast backlit architectural structure at dusk.

caption: The true cost of paying minimums on credit card debt. $3,000 at 24% APR takes 15 years if you only pay the minimum. #personalfinance #creditcards #debtfree #moneytok #quietmoney
description: Paying only the minimum on credit card debt keeps you trapped in high interest for years. Learn how a small increase in monthly payments saves thousands in interest.
first_comment: How much extra do you add to your card payments each month?

facts.claim: A $3,000 balance at 24% APR paying only the minimum takes 183 months (~15 years) and costs $4,887 in interest.
facts.basis: Fact sheet rule: $3,000 credit card at 24% APR paying only the minimum (1% + interest, min $25): 183 months (~15 years), $4,887 interest.

facts.claim: Paying $300 a month clears the $3,000 balance at 24% APR in 12 months with $381 interest.
facts.basis: Fact sheet rule: Same $3,000 at 24% paying $300/month: 12 months, $381 interest.
